subject: ing
title: Spanish verb times: one word or two?

points.heading: One-word verb times
points.body:
Today we learn how Spanish shows WHEN an action happens. A verb is an action word (**cantar** = to sing). To conjugate means to change that word for who speaks and for the time of the action. When we tell facts as real, we are in the indicative mood: we are narrating, not wishing.

## Key idea

Let's explore together. We start with simple tenses. «Simple» means the verb is ONE word. Think of five clocks: present (now/habit: canto), imperfect (ongoing or repeated past: cantaba), preterite (finished past: canté), future (later: cantaré), conditional (would: cantaría). The stem is what remains after dropping -ar/-er/-ir (**cantar** → cant-). The ending is the tip you add; changing it also changes the time.

Read the I-forms of **cantar** as one short story: canto (now) · cantaba (past, still open) · canté (past, closed) · cantaré (later) · cantaría (would).

## More examples
One-word clock: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**.
Two-word clock: **he cantado / había comido / habré vivido / habría terminado**.
Choose: «Yesterday I **finished**» (one closed word) vs «I **have finished** already» (two words).
Story mix: «I **was reading** when the phone **rang**.»

Practice: Now it's your turn. Write those five I-forms for cantar and for comer. Beside each one, note the «when» in your own words. Read them aloud in order.

Common mistake: Using cantaba when the event is fully finished. With a closed «yesterday», prefer canté.

History link: «**Colón llegó** en 1498» (one word, closed past) vs «**he llegado**» (two words).

points.heading: Two-word verb times
points.body:
Today we will walk through this idea step by step. Sometimes Spanish uses TWO words. That is a compound tense. Word one is a **helper** form of haber (he, has, ha…). Here haber does not mean «there is»; it is only a **helper** that changes with I/you/he. Word two is the participle: the «already done» form, usually ending in -ado or -ido (cantado, comido, vivido).

## Key idea

Let's explore together. Build he cantado slowly: he is the **helper**, cantado is the participle. Together they mean the singing already happened and still matters now. The participle stays still while the **helper** walks: yo he cantado, tú has cantado, él ha cantado.

## More examples
One-word clock: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**.
Two-word clock: **he cantado / había comido / habré vivido / habría terminado**.
Choose: «Yesterday I **finished**» (one closed word) vs «I **have finished** already» (two words).
Story mix: «I **was reading** when the phone **rang**.»

Practice: Now it's your turn. Write he / había / habré / habría + cantado. Circle the helper and underline the participle. Say aloud: «two pieces: helper + already-done form».

Common mistake: Writing hemos comidos. The participle does not take plural -s here → hemos comido.

points.heading: One word or two?
points.body:
Now we learn to choose. Ask: am I pointing to a clear closed moment, or to something already done whose result is still alive?

## Key idea

Let's explore together. Walk through three sentences with me. «Ayer terminé el libro» uses one word because yesterday closed. «Ya he terminado el libro» uses two words because the result still matters. «Leía cuando sonó el teléfono» sets a background (leía) and then a closed hit (sonó).

## More examples
One-word clock: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**.
Two-word clock: **he cantado / había comido / habré vivido / habría terminado**.
Choose: «Yesterday I **finished**» (one closed word) vs «I **have finished** already» (two words).
Story mix: «I **was reading** when the phone **rang**.»

Practice: Now it's your turn. Write three pairs with the same verb (one-word version and two-word version). Under each pair, explain your choice in half a line.

Common mistake: Forcing «Ayer he ido» when your home ear says «Ayer fui» for a closed yesterday.

lesson.summary: Learn to narrate WHEN an action happens: one-word forms and two-word forms (haber + already-done form), choosing with meaning.
lesson.memoryPhrase: One word: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**. Two words: helper **haber** + already-done form (**he cantado**).

questions.prompt: Which Spanish form shows an action happening now?
Which form tells about a finished action yesterday?

choices: A repeated or ongoing past action.
questions.answer: A repeated or ongoing past action.

questions.prompt: What two parts make a compound tense?
choices: A form of haber and a participle.
questions.answer: A form of haber and a participle.

questions.prompt: In «he cantado», which word is the participle?
Why should «comido» stay the same in «hemos comido»?
choices: It is always a future word.
The participle does not become plural for the subject.
questions.answer: The participle does not become plural for the subject.

questions.prompt: Which one-word Spanish form can mean «I sing»?
Choose the correct answer. **He cantado** has how many verb words?

choices: A repeated or ongoing past action.
questions.answer: A repeated or ongoing past action.

questions.prompt: What do you need to build a two-word Spanish tense?
choices: A form of haber and a participle.
questions.answer: A form of haber and a participle.

questions.prompt: Which word names the finished-form part?
What is the rule for the participle in this example?
choices: The participle does not become plural for the subject.
It is always a future word.
questions.answer: The participle does not become plural for the subject.

questions.prompt: Busca en el punto 1 («One-word verb times») y escribe entre comillas las palabras exactas donde la clase habla de esto: Yesterday I **finished**. Luego explica con tus palabras qué entendiste.
Copia entre comillas la frase exacta del punto 2 («Two-word verb times») que mejor resume la idea principal. Después explica por qué esa frase es importante.
En el punto 3 («One word or two?»), encuentra y copia entre comillas las palabras exactas relacionadas con: Ayer terminé el libro. Explica qué significa esa idea en la clase de hoy.
Escribe entre comillas una cita exacta del punto 1 («One-word verb times») que puedas usar para enseñarle a un compañero esta idea. Luego explica la cita con tus propias palabras.
